info.name: AI Customer Support Agent API
info.description:
REST API for the AI customer support chat app: JWT auth plus AI chat with history stored in MongoDB.

## Getting started
1. Start the server: `bun run --filter @support-agent/server dev` from the repository root (requires a filled-in `.env`).
2. Check `baseUrl` in the collection variables (default `http://localhost:4000`).
3. Run **Auth → Sign up** (or **Log in**). Postman stores the session cookie automatically, so every request after that is authenticated.
4. Run **Chat → Send message (new conversation)**. Its test script saves `conversationId` for the follow-up requests.
5. The Chat folder ends by deleting that conversation, so the collection can be run repeatedly.

## Resources
| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/signup` | Create an account and start a session |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/login` | Start a session |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/logout` | End the session |
| GET | `/api/v1/auth/me` | Current user |
| POST | `/api/v1/chat/send` | Send a message (optionally to an existing conversation) and get the AI reply |
| GET | `/api/v1/chat/history` | List conversations, with cursor pagination and title search |
| GET | `/api/v1/chat/history/:conversationId` | Get a conversation and its messages |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/chat/history/:conversationId` | Rename a conversation |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/chat/history/:conversationId` | Delete a conversation and its messages |
| POST | `/api/v1/chat/history/:conversationId/title` | Generate a title with the AI |

Run the whole collection top to bottom with the Collection Runner for a full end-to-end check.

## Authentication
Login and signup set an `httpOnly` cookie named `session` containing a JWT valid for 7 days. Routes under `/api/v1/auth/me` and `/api/v1/chat` require it.
Browser clients must send requests with `credentials: "include"` (fetch) or `withCredentials: true` (axios).

## Error format
Every error response has the same shape:
```json
{ "error": "Human readable message" }
```
Validation failures (400) also include `details` with `formErrors` and per-field `fieldErrors`.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 400 | Request body or URL parameter failed validation, or malformed JSON |
| 401 | Missing, invalid or expired session, or wrong credentials |
| 404 | Route or conversation not found (other users' conversations also return 404) |
| 409 | Email already registered |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded |
| 502 | The AI provider failed or returned an empty reply |
| 503 | The AI provider is rate limiting (common on free models) |

## Rate limits
- All routes: 100 requests per 15 minutes per IP.
- `POST /auth/signup` and `POST /auth/login`: 20 requests per 15 minutes per IP (shared).

Responses include `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers, and every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header that matches the server log line for that request.

request.description:
Sends a message to the AI assistant and stores both the user message and the reply.

Omit `conversationId` to start a new conversation. Its title starts as the first 60 characters of the message; call **Generate title** afterwards to replace it with a short AI-written title.
Nothing is stored if the AI call fails, so a failed send never leaves an empty conversation behind.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | 1 to 4000 characters after trimming |
| `conversationId` | string | Optional, id of one of your conversations |

Returns the conversation and the two new messages. The test script saves `conversation.id` as `conversationId` for the requests that follow.

Asks the AI for a short title based on the first messages of the conversation and saves it. Returns the updated conversation. If the AI is unavailable the current title is kept.

Updating the title does not change `updatedAt`, so the conversation keeps its place in the list.

request.description:
Returns one page of the user's conversations, most recently active first.

Pagination is cursor based. Each response has a `nextCursor`; pass it back as `cursor` to get the next page. `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page. Cursors are opaque, and conversations created or updated while paging never cause duplicates or skipped items.

| Query | Rules |
|---|---|
| `limit` | 1 to 50, default 20 |
| `q` | Optional title search, up to 100 characters |
| `cursor` | Optional, from a previous response |

The test script saves `nextCursor` so you can enable `cursor` and send again.
